Synopsis:
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish Jackson Hole speech, driving US 10-year Treasury yields to their highest since Trump's January 2025 inauguration. Warsh signaled the Fed has "work to do" on inflation and does not view current policy as meaningfully restrictive. Futures markets now price a ~67% chance of a rate hike at the upcoming September meeting. Compounding pressure: rising crude oil prices (Iran war escalation), BOJ and ECB also leaning toward hikes, Japan's 10-year JGB hitting 3% for the first time since 1996, and yen weakness. Equity markets are under pressure — US futures in the red, Hong Kong Hang Seng down 1%. Broadcom earnings are the key corporate event to watch.
